facts.text: The only player of the 1920s to throw for 1,500 yards was Benny Friedman — and he did it twice (1927: 1,721 yds; 1929: 1,700 yds).
The only player of the 1920s to carry the ball 200 times: Barney Wentz, 1926 — 220 carries.
The only player of the 1920s to throw 15 touchdown passes: Benny Friedman, 1929 — 20 TD, 11 INT.
The only player of the 1920s to return 3 punts for touchdowns: Curly Oden, 1926 — 3 PR TD.
Just four players of the 1920s threw 20 interceptions: Curly Lambeau (1924: 29 INT, 8 TD); Jack Ernst (1926: 21 INT, 1 TD); Wildcat Wilson (1928: 21 INT, 5 TD); Ernie Nevers (1926: 20 INT, 3 TD).
Most 1,000-yard passing seasons in the 1920s: Benny Friedman, 3 (1927, 1928, 1929).
Most 30-catch seasons in the 1920s: Charlie Mathys, 2 (1923, 1924).
Most 60-point seasons in the 1920s: Paddy Driscoll, 3 (1923, 1925, 1926).
Most 10-touchdown-pass seasons in the 1920s: Benny Friedman, 2 (1927, 1929).
Just three players of the 1920s ran for 10 touchdowns: Tex Hamer (1924: 12 rush TD); Ernie Nevers (1929: 12 rush TD); Barney Wentz (1926: 10 rush TD).
Just three players of the 1920s scored 12 touchdowns: Tex Hamer (1924: 12 TD); Ernie Nevers (1929: 12 TD); Len Sedbrook (1929: 12 TD).
Oldest player with a 1,000-yard passing season in the 1920s: Curly Lambeau, age 26 in 1924 (1,094).
Most interceptions thrown in a season in the 1920s: Curly Lambeau, 1924 — 29.
Most rushing yards in a season in the 1920s: Tex Hamer, 1924 — 789.
Oldest player with a 30-catch season in the 1920s: Jimmy Conzelman, age 29 in 1927 (36).
Youngest player with a 30-catch season in the 1920s: Charlie Berry, age 23 in 1925 (33).
Most catches in a season in the 1920s: Charley Rogers, 1927 — 38.
Most receiving yards in a season in the 1920s: Charlie Mathys, 1924 — 579.
Oldest player with a 60-point season in the 1920s: Paddy Driscoll, age 31 in 1926 (86).
Most points scored in a season in the 1920s: Paddy Driscoll, 1926 — 86.
Oldest player with an 8-touchdown season in the 1920s: Tony Latone, age 32 in 1929 (9).
Best yards per carry in a season (150+ carries) in the 1920s: Tony Latone, 1925 — 4.
Most all-purpose yards in a season in the 1920s: Charley Rogers, 1927 — 1,049.
Most carries in a season in the 1920s: Barney Wentz, 1926 — 220.
Oldest player with a 6-plus touchdown-catch season in the 1920s: Ray Flaherty, age 26 in 1929 (8).
Most touchdown catches in a season in the 1920s: Ray Flaherty, 1929 — 8.
Most yards from scrimmage in a season in the 1920s: Charley Rogers, 1927 — 1,049.
Best punting average in a season (40+ punts) in the 1920s: Verne Lewellen, 1929 — 41.9.
7 players threw for 800 yards with 8 or fewer touchdowns in the 1920s (10 seasons). The most extreme: Ernie Nevers, 1927 — 1,362 yds, 5 TD.
Youngest player with a 1,000-yard passing season in the 1920s: Benny Friedman, age 22 in 1927 (1,721).
Most passing yards in a season in the 1920s: Benny Friedman, 1927 — 1,721.
Youngest player with a 20-interception season as a passer in the 1920s: Ernie Nevers, age 24 in 1926 (20).
Youngest player with an 8-touchdown season in the 1920s: Tex Hamer, age 23 in 1924 (12).
Oldest player with a double-digit rushing touchdown season in the 1920s: Ernie Nevers, age 27 in 1929 (12).
Youngest player with a double-digit rushing touchdown season in the 1920s: Tex Hamer, age 23 in 1924 (12).
Oldest player with a 10-touchdown-pass season in the 1920s: Benny Friedman, age 24 in 1929 (20).
Youngest player with a 10-touchdown-pass season in the 1920s: Benny Friedman, age 22 in 1927 (11).
Most touchdown passes in a season in the 1920s: Benny Friedman, 1929 — 20.
Most rushing yards of the 1920s: Tony Latone, 2,365.
Most catches of the 1920s: Jimmy Conzelman, 99.
Most receiving yards of the 1920s: Charlie Mathys, 1,489.
Most touchdowns of the 1920s: Verne Lewellen, 35.
Most points scored in the 1920s: Paddy Driscoll, 377.
Most interceptions thrown in the 1920s: Curly Lambeau, 70.
Most passing yards of the 1920s: Benny Friedman, 4,769.
Most touchdown passes of the 1920s: Benny Friedman, 40.

method: NFL before 2000: each line is one Stathead (Pro Football Reference) Season Finder query over the decade, run in a signed-in subscriber session; the result rows, with Pro Football Reference's stable player ids, are stored as provenance. Nothing recalled or estimated.

Passing, rushing and receiving are official from 1932, interceptions from 1940, sacks from 1982 (Pro Football Reference's unofficial earlier sack counts are excluded); rules on a category a decade did not record simply return nothing. The 1960s include AFL seasons, which NFL records count; the 1940s exclude the AAFC, which they do not.
